summary: APT29, widely known as Cozy Bear, is a Russian state-sponsored cyberespionage group assessed to operate on behalf of Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), active since at least 2008 and linked to the 2016 DNC breach and the 2020 SolarWinds/Sunburst supply-chain attack.

title: Core Security Technologies
summary: Core Security Technologies is an information-security company founded in 1996 in Buenos Aires, Argentina, best known for creating the commercial penetration-testing platform Core Impact and for its long association with the open-source network-protocol toolkit Impacket.

title: CrowdStrike
summary: CrowdStrike is an American cybersecurity company founded in 2011 by George Kurtz, Dmitri Alperovitch, and Gregg Marston, known for its cloud-native Falcon endpoint protection platform and for its 2016 investigation attributing the Democratic National Committee hack to Russian state-linked groups.

title: Equation Group
summary: The Equation Group is a highly sophisticated cyberespionage actor publicly identified and named by Kaspersky Lab researchers in February 2015, whose tools, techniques, and operational details have led researchers and journalists to widely link it to the U.S. National Security Agency; a subset of its hacking tools was later stolen and leaked by a group calling itself the Shadow Brokers.

title: Hacking Team
summary: Hacking Team was a Milan-based company that sold offensive intrusion and surveillance software to governments and police forces worldwide, until a July 2015 breach by the hacker Phineas Fisher exposed roughly 400 gigabytes of its internal emails, source code, and client list.

title: Lazarus Group
summary: Lazarus Group is a state-sponsored cyber threat actor widely attributed to North Korea, active since at least 2009 and linked to the 2014 Sony Pictures hack, the 2016 Bangladesh Bank SWIFT heist, and the 2017 WannaCry ransomware outbreak.

title: Mandiant
summary: Mandiant is a cybersecurity firm specializing in incident response and threat intelligence, founded in 2004 by Kevin Mandia, best known for its 2013 "APT1" report publicly attributing years of cyber espionage against U.S. and other organizations to a Chinese military unit.

title: NSO Group
summary: NSO Group is an Israeli technology company, founded in 2010, best known for developing Pegasus, a commercial "zero-click" spyware suite sold to government clients and later linked to widespread surveillance of journalists, activists, lawyers, and political figures worldwide.

title: Zero Day Initiative (ZDI)
summary: The Zero Day Initiative (ZDI) is a vendor-agnostic vulnerability purchase and coordinated-disclosure program started on July 25, 2005 by TippingPoint, a division of 3Com, and led today by Trend Micro following its 2015 acquisition of HP TippingPoint.

title: Computer Underground Digest
summary: Computer Underground Digest (CuD) was a weekly electronic newsletter published from March 1990 to March 2000 that covered the legal, social, and cultural issues surrounding the early computer underground, edited by Jim Thomas with Gordon Meyer as news editor.

title: Countdown to Zero Day: Stuxnet and the Launch of the World's First Digital Weapon
summary: "Countdown to Zero Day" is a 2014 nonfiction book by American investigative journalist Kim Zetter, published by Crown, that chronicles the discovery and technical analysis of the Stuxnet computer worm and its sabotage of Iran's Natanz uranium-enrichment facility.

title: Ghost in the Wires: My Adventures as the World's Most Wanted Hacker
summary: "Ghost in the Wires" is a 2011 memoir by Kevin Mitnick, co-written with William L. Simon, recounting Mitnick's years as a computer intruder and phone phreaker, his time as a federal fugitive, and his 1995 arrest.

title: Kingpin: How One Hacker Took Over the Billion-Dollar Cybercrime Underground
summary: "Kingpin" is a 2011 non-fiction book by journalist and former hacker Kevin Poulsen, published by Crown, that chronicles the rise and fall of Max Ray Butler (a.k.a. "Max Vision" and "Iceman"), a hacker who stole access to roughly 1.8 million credit card accounts and took over rival carding forums to build the unified marketplace CardersMarket.

title: The RISKS Digest
summary: The RISKS Digest, formally the "Forum On Risks to the Public in Computers and Related Systems," is a moderated mailing list and Usenet newsgroup (comp.risks) documenting failures, vulnerabilities, and unintended consequences of computer systems, moderated by Peter G. Neumann since its founding on August 1, 1985.

title: Sandworm: A New Era of Cyberwar and the Hunt for the Kremlin's Most Dangerous Hackers
summary: "Sandworm" is a 2019 nonfiction book by American journalist Andy Greenberg, published by Doubleday, that chronicles the investigation into a Russian military-intelligence hacking group and its escalating cyberattacks, culminating in the 2017 NotPetya malware outbreak.

title: The Art of Deception
summary: "The Art of Deception: Controlling the Human Element of Security" is a 2002 book by former hacker Kevin D. Mitnick and co-author William L. Simon, published by John Wiley & Sons, that explains how social engineering is used to bypass technical security controls.

title: Binary Ninja
summary: Binary Ninja is a commercial interactive disassembler, decompiler, and binary analysis platform developed by Vector 35, first released publicly in July 2016 as an alternative to IDA Pro for reverse engineers.

title: Cain & Abel
summary: Cain & Abel was a free Windows password recovery and network analysis tool created by Italian developer Massimiliano Montoro, combining packet sniffing, ARP spoofing, and password-cracking techniques into a single application widely used for both legitimate security testing and credential theft during the 2000s and early 2010s.

title: Maltego
summary: Maltego is a graphical link-analysis and open-source intelligence (OSINT) platform, originally developed by the company Paterva (now Maltego Technologies GmbH), used to map relationships between people, organizations, domains, and other entities for security research, threat intelligence, and investigations.

title: OllyDbg
summary: OllyDbg is a 32-bit x86 assembler-level debugger for Microsoft Windows, created by Oleh Yuschuk, that became one of the most widely used tools of the 2000s for binary code analysis, reverse engineering, and malware analysis when source code is unavailable.

title: Responder
summary: Responder is an open-source LLMNR, NBT-NS, and mDNS poisoning tool created by Laurent Gaffié that stands up rogue authentication servers to capture NetNTLM hashes and cleartext credentials on local networks.

title: Sysinternals Suite
summary: Sysinternals is a suite of advanced Windows system-internals, diagnostic, and troubleshooting utilities — including Process Explorer, Autoruns, and Process Monitor — originally created by Mark Russinovich and Bryce Cogswell and acquired by Microsoft in 2006.

title: BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708)
summary: BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708) is a critical, wormable remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft's Remote Desktop Services affecting older Windows versions, disclosed and patched by Microsoft in May 2019.

title: Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966)
summary: Citrix Bleed (CVE-2023-4966) is a critical information-disclosure vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances that let remote attackers steal valid session tokens from device memory and hijack authenticated sessions, bypassing passwords and multi-factor authentication.

title: Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195)
summary: Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195) is a race-condition flaw in the Linux kernel's copy-on-write memory handling that let unprivileged local users gain write access to read-only memory mappings and escalate to root, publicly disclosed in October 2016 after evidence of active exploitation.

title: Follina (CVE-2022-30190)
summary: Follina (CVE-2022-30190) is a remote code execution vulnerability in the Microsoft Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT), triggered via the ms-msdt URL protocol handler from malicious Microsoft Office documents, publicly disclosed in May 2022.

title: ProxyLogon (CVE-2021-26855 and related)
summary: ProxyLogon is the name given to a chain of Microsoft Exchange Server vulnerabilities, led by the pre-authentication server-side request forgery flaw CVE-2021-26855, discovered by Orange Tsai of DEVCORE and exploited at mass scale by the Chinese state-sponsored group HAFNIUM in early 2021.

title: Rowhammer
summary: Rowhammer is a hardware vulnerability class in dense DRAM chips in which repeatedly and rapidly accessing ("hammering") a memory row can cause electrical interference that flips bits in adjacent rows, potentially altering data an attacker does not have permission to touch.

title: Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472)
summary: Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) is a critical cryptographic flaw in the Netlogon Remote Protocol used by Windows domain controllers, disclosed by Tom Tervoort of Secura in 2020, that let an unauthenticated attacker on the network take full control of an Active Directory domain.

title: POODLE (CVE-2014-3566)
summary: POODLE is a 2014 design vulnerability in SSL 3.0 that can allow a network attacker to recover plaintext from a connection forced to use the obsolete protocol.

title: FREAK (CVE-2015-0204)
summary: FREAK is a TLS weakness that could allow a network attacker to downgrade some connections to export-grade RSA encryption and factor the resulting weak key.

title: Badlock (CVE-2016-2118)
summary: Badlock is the public name for CVE-2016-2118, a Samba and Windows remote-protocol vulnerability disclosed in April 2016.

title: BlueBorne
summary: BlueBorne is a set of Bluetooth vulnerabilities disclosed by Armis in 2017 that affected implementations across Android, Windows, Linux, and older Apple platforms.

title: GHOST (CVE-2015-0235)
summary: GHOST is CVE-2015-0235, a heap-based buffer overflow in glibc name-resolution functions that affected older versions of the GNU C Library.

title: DROWN (CVE-2016-0800)
summary: DROWN is a 2016 cross-protocol attack that can use SSLv2 support to decrypt some TLS connections protected with the same RSA key.

title: EFAIL
summary: EFAIL is a class of attacks disclosed in 2018 that used weaknesses in some OpenPGP and S/MIME email-client handling to exfiltrate decrypted message content.

title: Spring4Shell (CVE-2022-22965)
summary: Spring4Shell is CVE-2022-22965, a Spring Framework data-binding vulnerability that could enable remote code execution in certain JDK 9+ and Tomcat WAR deployments.
